I only use cheap guitars, for the most part. Everything I have recorded lately has been on an 89 dollar Squier Strat. You don't need fancy guitars to sound good, you just need to play well.

In fact, I still have the price tag on this one.

https://imgur.com/gallery/FdUxYTU

Generally, I keep an eye out for functional Fenders at pawn shops. If I see a neck I like, or a good set of electronics, I take them apart and reassemble them to the most pleasing configuration. So, this Squier is a bit of a Frankenstein monster in that it has the classic fat headstock, HSH pickups and a super position switch. Once you fiddle with it, enough, it is better than anything you can buy in retail for a fraction of the price.

Also, if you don't like the pickup arrangements, you can order cheap knock offs that work just fine from China and they have no qualms about using the proprietary "noiseless" pickups that cost hundreds in the US for like 20 bucks. The first thing you do with a Fender is get rid of the 60 cycle hum and adding a humbucker to the mix is the quickest way to do that.

Point being... most of those guitars aren't junk, you just have to learn how to get the most out of them.

Also, a lot of people keep the tone and volume knobs turned way up which is generally incorrect. About 3/4 of the way helps eliminate a lot of fret noise.

The other thing I would recommend for people on a budget is to buy flat wound strings. They aren't as bright sounding, but they last for freaking ever. I, for one, don't like to waste my time changing strings a lot, so the flat wounds are a good solution and will save money for people who don't want to spend the 10 to 15 on a new set of strings every few weeks.
